key_insight: Modular surface-code architectures can remain fault-tolerant even when inter-module Bell-pair interfaces are significantly noisier than intra-QPU operations, and can support efficient distributed logical state preparation.
engineering_relevance: This work gives practical design guidance for scalable multi-QPU quantum systems by quantifying interface-noise tolerance and reducing the overhead of nonlocal logical gates and GHZ-state preparation.
method: Circuit-level simulations of fault-tolerant nonlocal CNOT gates using lattice surgery between QPUs connected by noisy Bell pairs
Rotated surface-code encoding to study logical error rates under intra-QPU and interface noise
Ancilla-overhead minimization for distributed GHZ preparation mapped to a vertex-cover problem with a polynomial-time heuristic
evidence_signal: The abstract reports quantitative simulations showing interface noise can be tolerated up to about an order of magnitude above intra-QPU noise with only a minor threshold reduction.
watch_item: The results depend on the assumed noisy Bell-pair interface model and heuristic ancilla selection, so hardware-specific performance may vary.
paper_title: Fault-Tolerant Logical Operations and Efficient State Preparation in Modular Quantum Architectures with Noisy Interfaces
